description: Machine-readable catalog/state requirements. This policy distinguishes visual components from composable factories and platform helpers. A public @Composable is counted as a visual API only when it renders UI on its own; everything matched by apiDocOnlyRules is documented via Dokka/API docs instead of a catalog card, and an existing genuine catalog mapping always wins over the api-doc-only classification.

apiDocOnlyRules.reason: Value holders, geometry/interaction helpers, and theme entry points. They compute or resolve values and render no pixels; the Foundation layer contains no @Composable that renders UI.

apiDocOnlyRules.match: layer in {atoms, molecules} and source file name contains 'Defaults'
apiDocOnlyRules.reason: Default parameter holders (StylishButtonDefaults/StylishCardDefaults/StylishControlDefaults object functions). They return style objects consumed by their component; the component's own demo carries the visual coverage.

apiDocOnlyRules.match: layer in {atoms, molecules} and name in {colors, shape, elevation, border}
apiDocOnlyRules.reason: Parameter-default provider composables declared next to their component. They resolve style objects only and render nothing on their own, so a catalog card would show whatever the caller passes in, not the API itself.

Headless Structure-layer layout hosts (Connected*Column/Row/Grid/Lazy*, ConnectedToggleRow, DataTableLayout). They arrange children and compute connection geometry but apply no visual styling - every item is delegated to a slot lambda rendered by a Finish component. Their Finish counterparts (StylishConnected*) all carry catalog demos.

Composable state factories allocating hoisted state objects (e.g. rememberStylishDateRangePickerState, rememberStylishDismissState). They have no visual output. When a demo genuinely instantiates the factory to drive its component, the mapping is kept - coverage is never downgraded.
